settings.copy: A real bookshop is a conversation, not a transaction. Holloway & Page has spent nearly fifty years matching curious readers with the books they didn't know they were looking for — new hardcovers, dog-eared paperbacks, and a staff who read on their lunch breaks.

settings.title: More than
settings.intro: Anyone can sell you a book. We'd rather hand you the right one. Here's what that means in practice.

features.title: Staff picks with opinions
features.text: Every recommendation card on our shelves is written by someone who actually read the book. If we disliked it, we say so. No ghostwritten blurbs, no paid placement.

features.title: Small presses first
features.text: We champion independent and translated publishers the big chains overlook. Half our front table is given over to voices you won't find in a supermarket aisle.

features.title: The rare & out-of-print
features.text: A corner of the shop is given to first editions, out-of-print titles, and signed copies. If we don't have it, we'll hunt it down for you.

features.title: Readers, not just customers
features.text: Our reader-club, book groups, and author evenings mean the shop is a meeting place, not a warehouse. Come for the stock, stay for the conversation.
features.detail: Monthly author events in our reading room

features.title: Order it, we'll find it
features.text: Can't see it? Tell us the title and we'll order it, usually within a week — at the list price, no markup, no fuss.
features.detail: Free in-shop pickup on all orders

settings.title: Forty-eight years
settings.intro: Holloway & Page has changed hands once and kept its soul twice. Here's how we got here.

events.title: A shop opens on Main Street
events.text: Margaret Holloway takes over a bankrupt newsagent's and fills it, floor to ceiling, with paperbacks. The shop has its first paying customer before the sign goes up.

events.title: The rare-books corner
events.text: A customer brings in a box of first editions and refuses to sell them to anyone but Margaret. The glass-fronted corner is born — and never empty again.

events.title: A second generation
events.text: Margaret's daughter, Ellen Page, takes over the shop and the name becomes Holloway & Page. The handover happens over a pot of tea at the back counter.

events.title: The reading room opens
events.text: We knock through into the next-door building to add a wood-panelled reading room for book groups, author evenings, and the slow act of finishing a chapter.

events.title: Still independent
events.text: Two chains have opened across the street and we're still here, ordering small presses, writing notes by hand, and selling the right book to the right reader.

settings.title: Wander the
settings.intro: A look at the nooks, shelves, and corners that make Holloway & Page feel less like a store and more like a very large, very well-read living room.
